clue.text: Show with established soprano that is gold — the ultimate in Broadway

parts.note: EST is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs
S is the abbreviation for soprano in vocal scores
id est is the Latin for 'that is', usually shortened to i.e.
OR is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its final letter, here taken from Broadway

explanation.surface: A description of a Broadway show with a soprano star dripping in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is written out in full Latin, ID EST, not the usual IE. The answer is linked across two lights, 1 and 5 across.
explanation.definitionFit: This Bernstein and Sondheim musical is a celebrated stage production, so it is a show.

clue.text: Western conspiracy nutter starts to taunt super-rich Gates

parts.note: David Icke is a well-known British conspiracy theorist

indicators.note: starts to means only the opening letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A conspiracy crank begins mocking the billionaire Bill Gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gates' looks like Bill Gates, given 'super-rich'; it is the definition. In cricket the wicket is the set of stumps, and an old sense of wicket is a small gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicket is a small door or gate, especially one set into a larger gate.

clue.text: 17 Fleet St tradesman

parts.note: 17 refers to the answer to 17 down, savage; the musical's anti-hero is a murderous barber with a shop in Fleet Street

explanation.surface: A vicious shopkeeper on the London street once home to the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street is a London street long associated with the press. Read the 17 as the answer to 17 down: the demon barber of Fleet Street is a savage tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: This fictional barber, star of Sondheim's musical, slits customers' throats in his Fleet Street shop.

clue.text: Work of famous compiler: ten down "Chinless bastard"

indicators.note: bastard as an adjective means corrupted or debased, so the letters of the words before it are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: A setter's clue reading as a crude insult aimed at someone with a weak chin.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'compiler' is Sondheim, who also set cryptic crosswords; 'ten down' looks like a cross-reference but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This ballad from A Little Night Music is the best-known song by Sondheim, who also compiled crosswords.

clue.text: Con artist enemy of Batman changing US party allegiance initially

indicators.note: switching parties in the US means a Republican becoming a Democrat, so the initial for one swaps for the initial of the other

parts.note: the Riddler is one of Batman's villains

explanation.surface: A swindling Batman villain who switches American political parties.
explanation.walkthrough: R (Republican) is replaced by D (Democrat) at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A diddler is a cheat or swindler, from the informal verb diddle, to trick someone out of money.

clue.text: See 1
He opens the mind in a creative way, embodying singular genius

indicators.note: embodying means holding the next piece within itself
in a creative way means the letters are rearranged inventively

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A tribute to a brilliant artist who broadens the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a creative way' rearranges HEOPENSTHEMIND, and 'embodying' takes S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer and lyricist is widely hailed as a towering talent of musical theatre.

clue.text: Golf GTI shedding the odd bits frequently

indicators.note: shedding the odd bits means dropping the first, third, fifth and seventh letters, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A VW Golf GTI often loses odd parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the even letters of GOLFGTI: O, F, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Oft is a poetic or archaic word for often.

clue.text: Longed for Geordie to do a turn at Hogmanay

indicators.note: to do a turn means the two letters for the Geordie's region are turned around in place

parts.note: longed for means yearned
a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: A Geordie who longed to perform a turn at the Scottish New Year party.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogmanay is the Scottish celebration of New Year's Eve. Geordies come from Newcastle, in the North East. 'to do a turn' flips NE in YEARNED to EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay falls on 31 December, the very end of the calendar year.

clue.text: Like Knutsville named after Knut? Knut raised about £25

indicators.note: about means the reversed piece goes round the next
in a down clue raised means read upwards, so the setter's word for himself is reversed

parts.note: Knut is the setter, so the setter refers to himself as me
a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: The setter imagines a town named after himself and pockets twenty-five pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ME into EM, which goes 'about' PONY. Pony is British money slang for £25.
explanation.definitionFit: Knut would be the eponym of Knutsville: an eponym is the person a place or thing is named after.

clue.text: Made a fortune, having been in Bath

definitions.meaning: to clean up is an idiom for making a lot of money
someone who has been in the bath has literally ..., i.e. washed

explanation.surface: Someone struck it rich while staying in the spa city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Bath look like the English spa city; it is just a bathtub.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning up is slang for winning big, and also literally washing oneself.

clue.text: Minor actor that's listed in the book along with 1D?

definitions.meaning: a film or stage performer in a non-speaking background role

definitions.text: that's listed in the book along with 1D?
definitions.meaning: in cricket, ... (byes, wides, no-balls) are recorded in the scorebook alongside the wickets that fell

explanation.surface: A bit-part player whose name appears in the cast book next to another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 1D is WICKETS: in a cricket scorebook, extras are runs not scored off the bat, and they are totalled beside the fall of wickets.
explanation.definitionFit: Background performers are called extras; in cricket, extras are runs credited without the batter hitting the ball.

clue.text: Burden, nuisance, a feeling of listlessness within

indicators.note: within says the answer sits inside the run of letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A list of burdens and nuisances that leave someone feeling flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' picks the letters out of burdEN NUIsance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is weary boredom, a French borrowing for a jaded lack of energy or interest.

clue.text: Jazz legend's more slimmed-down trumpet sound?

indicators.note: the question mark and sound say the phrase is to be spoken, giving a name that is pronounced alike

parts.note: more slimmed-down means LEANER, and a trumpet is a HORN

explanation.surface: Musing whether a jazz great's tone comes from a thinner trumpet.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is read as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay. LEANER HORN, said aloud, gives the singer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lena Horne was a celebrated American jazz singer and actress, so she is a jazz legend.

clue.text: Reforming Temperance League, at first secured successor

indicators.note: reforming means forming again, so the letters are put into a new shape
at first takes just the opening letter of League

explanation.surface: A reform movement for abstinence finds itself a new leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reforming' looks like describing the league's politics; it rearranges TEMPERANCE plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: A replacement is someone who takes over from another, filling the vacated role.

clue.text: Dodgy lawyer retiring, rest ordered

parts.note: retiring in the sense of bashful means shy

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of rest are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A crooked lawyer is stepping down, and has been told to take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like stepping down from work, but means bashful. 'ordered' turns REST into STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is slang for an unscrupulous, disreputable lawyer who uses sharp practice.

clue.text: Married Yoko, proud every now and then to get out camera attachment

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married, as in genealogies
Yoko Ono, the artist who was married to John Lennon

indicators.note: every now and then picks alternate letters from proud, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A married Yoko, proud of her outing, takes a camera accessory along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every now and then' takes P, O and D from proud.
explanation.definitionFit: A monopod is a single-legged support used to steady a camera, a one-legged tripod.

clue.text: France reduces growth expected next spring

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
to reduce something is to lower it

explanation.surface: France is cutting back the growth predicted for next year.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like an economic forecast; 'growth' is plant growth, and 'spring' the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Blooms are plant growth that gardeners look forward to appearing when the warm season returns.

clue.text: Foreign Office spreads untruths about Liberal vanity projects

indicators.note: about means going round, so the letters wrap the Liberal piece

parts.note: untruths are lies

explanation.surface: The Foreign Office spreading lies about a Liberal's pet schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreads' is only a link in the surface; 'about' puts the Liberal letter into the gap between the two other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A folly is an extravagant, useless building put up for show, so a vanity project.

clue.text: Wild herb found around Virginia

indicators.note: found around means the herb is put round the next piece

parts.note: sage is a herb
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A herb growing wild somewhere in Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' looks like it describes the herb, but it is the definition; 'found around' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage means untamed or fierce, as of an animal living in nature.

clue.text: Capri; so terribly dull

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of Capri and so are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A jaded traveller's verdict that the island of Capri is terribly boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' reworks CAPRISO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means lacking imagination or poetic beauty, so commonplace and unexciting.

clue.text: How I got my nuts crushed? Cheapest lederhosen trousers

definitions.text: How I got my nuts crushed?

indicators.note: trousers is read as a verb, to pocket or hold, so the answer is held within the words

explanation.surface: A painful complaint about cheap leather shorts that squeeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb meaning pockets: the answer is held in cheaPEST LEDerhosen. The definition is a joke: nuts crushed with a pestle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts ground in a mortar are pestled, pounded with a club-shaped tool.

clue.text: Carbon monoxide poisoning's beginning to permeate numerous soldiers

parts.note: CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide

indicators.note: to permeate means to get inside, so that letter goes into the word for numerous

parts.note: numerous means many

indicators.note: beginning means just the opening letter of poisoning's

explanation.surface: Carbon monoxide gas seeping into a large body of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to permeate' puts P inside MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is a military unit of soldiers, usually commanded by a captain or major.

clue.text: Boy! Saint-Laurent admits 50 old mistresses!

parts.note: a boy is a lad

indicators.note: admits means YVES lets other letters come inside it

parts.note: Yves Saint-Laurent was the French fashion designer
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A gossipy exclamation that the designer Saint-Laurent confesses to fifty past mistresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' puts the letters for 50 and old inside the designer's first name, giving YLOVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady-loves is an old-fashioned term for sweethearts, women who are loved by men.

clue.text: Crazy about … about … about vision

indicators.note: this about means going round, so the reversed word wraps the other piece
here about means turned round, so the word for crazy is read backwards

parts.note: crazy means mad
RE is the Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: A dazed, rambling line about some vision that someone is mad about.
explanation.walkthrough: The three 'about's each do a different job: the first reverses the word for crazy to give DAM, the second is the Latin-derived word for concerning, the third puts that inside DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is a vision seen in sleep, or an imagined ideal.

clue.text: Tiny flaws exposed part of one's extended family

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of the outer covering, so each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Small faults revealed in a relation by marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips the ends from tINy and fLAWs.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-law is a relative by marriage, such as a spouse's parent, so family beyond blood kin.

clue.text: US airport weak on security?

definitions.meaning: The code for Los Angeles International Airport
... means slack or careless, as in ... security

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks if an American airport has poor security.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Angeles International's three-letter code is the word for slack or negligent.

clue.text: Game Leander played in halcyon days?

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game

indicators.note: played suggests the letters of Leander are moved about like pieces in a game

explanation.surface: Recalling the glory days of a sporting club called Leander.
explanation.walkthrough: Leander is a famous rowing club at Henley, which helps the surface. 'played' reworks LEANDER to LDENERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Halcyon days are a past period of happiness and success, which a golden era is.

clue.text: Son cuts reeds

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees
axes, as a verb, means cuts

explanation.surface: A boy chopping down plants in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reeds' looks like plants but means reed instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxophones are reed instruments, and players call them reeds.

clue.text: Measurement of distance covered by assembling Tory demo

indicators.note: assembling means putting the letters of Tory demo together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Gauging how far a Conservative protest march has walked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembling' rearranges TORYDEMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Odometry is the use of motion data to estimate how far something has travelled, as an odometer does.
